result.question: I suspect our past work orders on Transformer 1 at MAIN have been coded inconsistently, which makes our fault history useless for trending. Pull all work orders on Transformer 1, open and closed, and show me each one's number, description, status and failure code. Then read our failure code catalog and map each code to the closest transformer fault class or failure mode: partial discharge, low-energy arcing, high-energy arcing, oil overheating, core/winding thermal, tap changer wear, moisture ingress, cellulose ageing or oil dielectric degradation. Flag every work order whose code doesn't match its description, and every one that has no code at all, and suggest the correct code for each. Also run a fault classification on the latest oil sample and tell me whether any open work order is coded for a different fault than the gases currently indicate. Only propose recodes, and don't change anything yourself unless the work order is still open and the description clearly names the fault. In that case, update its failure code and list what you changed. If the catalog has no code that fits a fault class, say so and recommend a new code rather than forcing a poor match.
result.answer:
## Work orders: Transformer 1, MAIN

Queried all statuses with no date restriction. **Only one work order was returned; no closed orders were found.**

| Number | Description | Status | Failure code | Audit finding / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | Transformer 1 - 2-day outage and transformer/OLTC inspection, 2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21 | WAPPR — open | None | **Missing code.** Inspection does not clearly name a fault. Leave unchanged pending diagnosis; if oil overheating is confirmed, FC006 fits broadly, but a dedicated transformer thermal code would improve trending. |

An OLTC inspection does **not** establish tap changer wear.

## Failure-code catalog mapping

The catalog contains generic symptoms, not transformer-specific fault classes.

| Code | Catalog description | Closest defensible transformer mapping |
|---|---|---|
| FC001 | Equipment does not start | None—nonspecific symptom |
| FC002 | Equipment stops unexpectedly during operation | None—nonspecific symptom |
| FC003 | Abnormal noise during operation | None—does not establish arcing or tap changer wear |
| FC004 | Fluid leak observed | None—oil leakage does not establish moisture ingress |
| FC005 | Excessive vibration, shaking, or instability | None—does not establish core/winding thermal failure |
| FC006 | Overheating or high temperature reading | **Oil overheating or core/winding thermal**, without distinguishing them |
| FC007 | Indicator light does not illuminate | None—instrumentation symptom |
| FC008 | Gauge does not operate or is inaccurate | None—instrumentation symptom |
| FC009 | Structural damage or cracking | None—does not establish moisture ingress or dielectric degradation |
| FC010 | Part missing or loose | None—does not establish tap changer wear |

**Recommended new codes—not created:** `TR-PD`, `TR-ARC-LOW`, `TR-ARC-HIGH`, `TR-OIL-THERMAL`, `TR-CORE-WINDING-THERMAL`, `TR-TAP-WEAR`, `TR-MOISTURE`, `TR-CELLULOSE-AGE`, and `TR-OIL-DIELECTRIC`. FC006 is a broad thermal match; the other classes have no suitable catalog code.

## Latest oil-sample classification

Latest available sample: **2024-01-19**, not a current-condition measurement.

Gas concentrations: H₂ **2,850**, CH₄ **7,400**, C₂H₆ **5,470**, C₂H₄ **16,650**, C₂H₂ **7 ppm**.

The classification tool failed with **“LLM unavailable.”** Manual ratio assessment gives:

- CH₄/H₂ = **2.596**
- C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = **0.000420**
- C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = **3.044**

These indicate **high-temperature thermal decomposition of oil, consistent with T3 (>700°C)**, rather than partial discharge or arcing. This is an inferred fault-zone temperature, not measured bulk oil temperature; gases alone do not locate the fault in the core, winding, or tap changer.

**Open-order comparison:** No open order is coded for a different fault—the only order has **no code**. Its inspection scope is not itself a conflicting diagnosis.

**Changes made: none.** The open order’s description does not clearly name a fault, so it did not meet your condition for automatic recoding.
